question: What is the primary advantage of the oral route for medication administration?

options.C: It provides the fastest drug absorption
options.D: It is completely free of side effects

explanation: Oral medications are simple to administer and inexpensive compared to parenteral routes, making them the preferred choice when feasible. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: A patient with which condition should be withheld oral medications until further assessment?
explanation: An absent gag reflex places the patient at high risk of aspiration if given anything by mouth. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: How many unique patient identifiers must a nurse check before giving medication?
explanation: Using two unique identifiers like name and hospital ID number prevents mixing up patients with similar names. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h2)

question: Checking the medication label against the order three times serves what main purpose?
explanation: The triple-check method catches discrepancies in drug selection, dosing, and labeling before the drug reaches the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h2)

question: What tool should be used to measure liquid oral medications accurately?
explanation: Calibrated oral syringes and medicine cups provide exact measurements, whereas household spoons vary widely in capacity. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: Why should sustained-release tablets never be crushed for oral administration?

options.A: It alters the drug release rate and causes toxicity
options.B: It causes the powder to harden in the cup
options.C: It inactivates the chemical ingredients instantly
options.D: It makes the medication taste extremely bitter

explanation: Crushing sustained-release medications releases the entire dose at once, which can lead to dangerous overdose levels in the blood. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h3)

question: What is the correct patient posture for swallowing oral medications safely?
explanation: An upright 90-degree sitting position uses gravity to assist swallowing and prevents aspiration into the airway. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h4)

question: What action must a nurse take if a patient refuses a prescribed oral medication?

options.A: Hide the medication inside the patient's meal
options.B: Document the refusal and report to the physician
options.C: Leave the pills on the bedside table for later
options.D: Force the patient to swallow the pills anyway

explanation: Competent patients have the right to refuse treatment; the nurse must document this refusal and inform the prescriber. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h4)

question: Why should nurses avoid mixing children's daily medications into essential foods like milk?

options.A: The child might develop an aversion to that staple food
options.B: Milk chemically neutralizes all pediatric medications
options.C: Essential foods lose all of their vitamins
options.D: The mixture will instantly solidify in the cup

explanation: Mixing drugs into essential foods can cause the child to reject healthy meals if they associate the food with medicine taste. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h5)

question: A major challenge commonly managed when giving oral drugs to older adults is:

options.B: Rapid metabolism of all tablet types

explanation: Older adults often take multiple drugs simultaneously and may struggle with swallowing due to age-related changes. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h5)

question: When is the most appropriate time to document administered oral medications?

options.B: At the end of the entire shift

explanation: Documenting right after administration prevents accidental double-dosing and ensures an accurate medical record. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why is post-administration monitoring an essential part of the medication procedure?

options.A: To check for therapeutic response and adverse reactions
options.B: To replace missing pills from the pharmacy stock
options.C: To calculate the total cost of the prescription
options.D: To fulfill mandatory hospital cleaning schedules

explanation: Observing the patient ensures the drug is working as intended and catches early signs of allergic reactions or side effects. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h6)
